No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Nigeria Cannot Afford Atiku’s Education Privatisation Agenda-Oshiomhole by Henry Tyohemba 4 seconds ago in Education Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Former Edo State Governor, Adams Oshiomhole, has said Nigeria cannot afford the education privatisation agenda being advocated by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Oshiomhole stated this on Monday at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa. He recalled that Atiku had pursued a privatisation agenda while serving as Vice-President, questioning the rationale behind advocating private-sector control of tertiary education in a country where millions of children still lack access to basic education. The former governor challenged opposition politicians, particularly Atiku and Peter Obi, to clarify whether they would retain or abolish the current education policies if elected into office. Oshiomhole also criticised Atiku over comments he attributed to the former Vice-President regarding the use of public resources to enrich friends, arguing that such an approach could undermine funding for education and student support programmes. “If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said. Earlier, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said the Federal Government had provided funding arrangements for its education data infrastructure and introduced a three-year renegotiation window in the agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and other university-based unions. He said the agreement could be reviewed every three years to prevent prolonged disputes over staff welfare and remuneration. The Minister of State for Education, Prof Suwaiba Said Ahmad, said the Ministry was also strengthening the education system through guidelines for appointing vice-chancellors, rectors and provosts, as well as policies addressing bullying in schools.
